newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Abbey profits helped by mortgages.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Abbey profits helped by mortgages.

text.p: Profits at Britain's fifth largest bank Abbey National Plc are likely to have got a boost in 1996 by an improvement in the UK mortgage market, analysts said.

Abbey shares took a tumble early this year as some analysts cut their recommendations after the stock had been on a bull run which in its turn, led to some securities houses recommending a purchase of the shares.
The Abbey is in the midst of bidding for mutually-owned life assurance firm Scottish Amicable and the market will be looking for clues as to the bank's intentions in next Thursday's announcement.

ScotAm on Thursday asked for firm offers to be tabled by the end of the month. Abbey has so far made a preliminary bid of 1.4 billion stg which it has said could increase once it has seen the ScotAm figures.
In any case, it will have to since the Abbey offer has already been trumped by Prudential Corp.
As far as pretax profits are concerned, estimates focus around the 1.17 billion stg area, after 1.026 billion in 1995.
Analysts expect a dividend pay-out of at least 26p per share in 1996 compared to 21.75p in 1995.
The Abbey is known to have cut back on its cut-price mortgage offers in the second half but higher volumes generally mean its market share will hardly be diminished.

Consumer credit, as seen elsewhere in the sector, is expected to have provided healthy growth and profits will also be higher from its treasury business although some analysts have doubts about the latter's long-term ability to add value.

The Abbey's capital position, with a tier one ratio of well above eight percent, is likely to lead to generous dividend payments since its management seems set against share repurchases although some analysts see the possibility of a special dividend as early as next week.
